meta.description: Yasakia is the dating app where you talk first: an AI agent gets to know you, then opens a small batch of people who fit you both ways. In construction.

home.title: Talk first. Meet both ways.
home.eyebrow: The dating app where you talk first
home.lead: No swipe, no catalogue, no score. An agent gets to know you in your own words, then opens a small batch of people who fit you in both directions.
home.principlesLead: What Yasakia refuses is as important as what it does.

talk.title: A conversation, not a form
talk.text: The agent asks one question at a time, with humour, in your language.

batch.title: Three to five people, not a feed
batch.text: A small batch, each with why you two in words — never a score.

both.title: Both ways, or not at all
both.text: Someone appears only if you fit them and they fit you.

debrief.title: The next batch waits for you
debrief.text: You debrief the last one first, so every batch fits better than the one before.

home.closingLead: Yasakia is open source, on the same foundations as Orochia and Orazaka. Read the code, or tell us what you expect from a dating app.

works.label: What works today
works.lead: Not released yet, but these parts already run in the code, tested in the code.

location.title: Your location, about 1 km
location.text: A phone's position is rounded to a grid of about 1 km before it is stored. The exact one never reaches the database.

radius.title: Matching inside the radius you choose
radius.text: You set the distance you accept, in kilometres. Matching uses PostgreSQL's earthdistance on the stored position.

signin.title: Sign in by e-mail code or password
signin.text: A 6-digit code arrives by e-mail, or sign in with a password. A forgotten password is reset by code, and every other session ends.

talk.title: An agent you talk to first
talk.text: One question at a time, in your language, in your own words — no form, no swipe. What it understood is shown back to you, the sensitive part sealed.

portrait.title: A portrait in words, never a score
portrait.text: When it knows enough, the agent writes who you are and who you look for, and embeds both. You can read it.

batch.title: Your first batch, three to five people
batch.text: People who fit you and for whom you fit too — the weaker of the two directions decides — each with why you two, in words. Fewer than three: you wait, nobody is made up.

debrief.title: Answering a batch and the debrief
debrief.text: Saying how it went so the next batch fits better is being built; it is not released yet.

intros.title: Introductions
intros.text: Seven days to talk when you both say yes: being built; it is not released yet.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: The whole loop, from the first question to the first message — what the app is built to do.

talk.title: 1 · You talk
talk.text: An AI agent gets to know you, one question at a time, in your language. It runs on Orazaka, Krizaka's sovereign AI.

batch.title: 2 · A small batch opens
batch.text: Three to five people, never a catalogue. Each comes with the reasons you two fit, written in words.

both.title: 3 · It goes both ways
both.text: Filters and fit are checked in both directions: nobody is shown to someone who would not be shown to them.

debrief.title: 4 · You debrief
debrief.text: Tell the agent what you thought of the batch. The next one waits for that debrief, and fits better.

privacy.position: Your position is rounded to about one kilometre before it is stored.
privacy.photos: Photos are re-encoded to strip every metadata block, GPS included, and shown only to someone in your batch or your intro, through a link that expires in minutes.
privacy.encrypted: Sensitive answers are encrypted at rest.
privacy.control: Export and deletion of your data are in the API from day one; blocks and reports work at once.
privacy.honest: No demo mode and no fake profile: where there is nothing real, nothing is shown.

how.stackLead: One database does the heavy lifting; no broker, no swipe engine.

stack.db: PostgreSQL with pgvector for who you are and who you seek, and the radius.
stack.ui: Krizaka UI, web and native — the same components as the other Krizaka products.
stack.ai: Orazaka for the agent; it never leaves Krizaka's own stack.

demo.title: Demo
demo.lead: Recorded on the development site, against the real engine: a test persona talks to the agent until it has written her portrait, then opens her first batch. Not an animation, not a mock-up — and not edited, only cut to these two moments and sped up while the agent thinks.
demo.talkLead: The agent gets to know her, one question at a time. It writes down what she said — nothing more — then her portrait.
demo.batchLead: People who fit her and for whom she fits too, each with why you two, in words, both ways.
demo.talkLabel: Recording: a person talks to the agent, which writes what it understood and then her portrait.
demo.batchLabel: Recording: the agent opens a batch of five people, each with the reasons you two fit, in words.

cues.open: Camille — a test persona, a fictional adult — signs in and opens the talk. She speaks first.
cues.first: She says who she is and where she lives. The agent answers with a question, not a form.
cues.range: She says whom she hopes to meet: an age range, a distance, a serious relationship.
cues.saturday: A perfect Saturday, what matters to her. The agent writes down what she said, and nothing more.
cues.enough: Five messages in, the agent has the basics and who she hopes to meet: it knows enough.
cues.portrait: Her portrait is written, in words, from what she said — and embedded by Orazaka: who she is, who she looks for.

cues.open: She asks for her first batch. The agent looks for people who fit her and for whom she fits too.
cues.looking: The filters work both ways, then the weaker of the two directions ranks. The agent writes why you two, one person after the other.
cues.shown: Five people, each with why you two — in words, both ways. No score, no swiping. They are a cast of fictional people made for tests.

demo.note: Camille is a test persona and the five people she meets are a fictional cast: nobody here exists, there is no photo, and Yasakia has no members. The agent's words are generated live by Orazaka — the model is not scripted — so a run differs from the next. Answering a batch, the debrief and the introductions are not built yet.
demo.nextText: Its own recording, made on the real application, replaces these. Until then: the code is public.
